On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. The pocket sits between Clarke Road and the Burnaby city line, on Glenayre Drive and its side streets; the adjoining Seaview sub-area is described by the City as extending from College Park Way to Ingersoll Street and from Seaforth Way to Glenayre Drive.
École Glenayre Elementary, at 495 Glencoe Drive, and the Glenayre Centre, at 492 Glencoe Drive, are the two named public buildings inside the pocket.
The stock is detached houses on Glenayre Drive and its side streets between Clarke Road and the Burnaby line, under the RS zones of Zoning Bylaw No. 2937.
The pocket's civic core is a school-and-centre pair on one street: École Glenayre Elementary at 495 Glencoe Drive and the Glenayre Centre at 492 Glencoe Drive face each other across Glencoe Drive.

blocks.text: Glenayre Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The RS1-S small-lot rezoning route is not offered in Glenayre: the City's list is Moody Centre, Seaview and Pleasantside only, so Glenayre lots use the standard RS rules and small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) instead.
Small-scale multi-unit housing is permitted in the RS and RT zones outside the City's transit-oriented areas, under the provincial housing legislation the City has implemented.
Port Moody is inside the speculation and vacancy tax taxable area, so residential owners here must declare each year.

blocks.text: Glenayre Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Glencoe Drive holds both of the pocket's public buildings within a few civic numbers of each other — 492 for the centre, 495 for the school — so the pocket's services are a single short street.
Seaview's stated extent uses Glenayre Drive as its south line (Seaforth Way to Glenayre Drive), so Glenayre Drive is a boundary street for the neighbouring sub-area as well as this pocket's spine.
The Burnaby line is the pocket's west edge, making Glenayre the Port Moody neighbourhood a Burnaby buyer crosses into first on this side of the city.
Port Moody property taxes are set city-wide, and the speculation and vacancy tax applies in Port Moody, so owners declare annually.
Clarke Road is the pocket's south route and Glenayre Drive its spine, tying the side streets to the Barnet Highway (Highway 7A) and St. Johns Street corridor.
College Park adjoins to the east and Seaview to the north-east, so the west-end neighbourhoods share one street system up to the Burnaby line.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Glenayre?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 9 houses listed in Glenayre. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Glenayre a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Glenayre had a sales ratio of 33% on only 9 listed, too few to read as a market type. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Glenayre from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 6 houses sold in Glenayre over those 5 months, out of 64 in all of Port Moody.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Glenayre?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.
École Glenayre Elementary, at 495 Glencoe Drive, is the pocket's own School District No.

faq.q: What recreation is inside the pocket?
faq.a: The Glenayre Centre, at 492 Glencoe Drive, is the City recreation facility inside the pocket, listed on the City's recreation facilities and locations page.

faq.q: Is Glenayre in Burnaby or Port Moody?
faq.a: Port Moody: the pocket sits between Clarke Road and the Burnaby city line, so its west edge touches Burnaby while its taxes, permits and bylaws are the City of Port Moody's under the Port Moody 2050 Official Community Plan.
